chunks.text: The majority of UMAP servicemen were conscientious objectors.

chunks.text: A small portion or about 8% to 9% of the immates were homosexual men, Jehovah's Witnesses, Seventh-day Adventists, Catholic priests and Protestant ministers, intellectuals, farmers who resisted collectivization, as well as anyone else considered "anti-social" or "counter-revolutionary."

chunks.text: Former Intelligence Directorate agent Norberto Fuentes estimated that of approximately 35,000 internees, 507 ended up in psychiatric wards, 72 died from torture, and 180 committed suicide.

chunks.text: A 1967 human rights report from the Organization of American States found that over 30,000 internees are "forced to work for free in state farms from 10 to 12 hours a day, from sunrise to sunset, seven days per week, poor alimentation with rice and spoiled food, unhealthy water, unclean plates, congested barracks, no electricity, latrines, no showers, immates are given the same treatment as political prisoners."
chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production

chunks.text: The report concludes that the UMAP camps’ two objectives are "facilitating free labor for the state" and "punishing young people who refuse to join communist organizations."
chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production

chunks.text: The Cuban government maintained that the UMAPs are not labor camps, but part of military service.
chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production

chunks.text: In a 2010 interview with "La Jornada", Fidel Castro admitted in response to a question about the UMAP camps that "Yes, there were moments of great injustice, great injustice!"

chunks.text: A pelletron is a type of electrostatic particle accelerator similar to a Van de Graaff generator.

chunks.text: Pelletrons have been built in many sizes, from small units producing voltages up to 500 kilovolts (kV) and beam energies up to 1 megaelectronvolt (MeV) of kinetic energy, to the largest system, which has reached a DC voltage of over 25 megavolts and produced ion beams with energies over 900 MeV.
chunks.title: Pelletron

chunks.text: Generating electric charge is done by a mechanical transportation system made of a chain of pellets (short conductive tubes connected by links made of insulating material), that is used to build up high voltages on the Pelletron terminal.
chunks.title: Pelletron

chunks.text: The system is enclosed by a pressure vessel filled with insulating gas, such as SF (sulfur hexafluoride), and an evacuated beamline.
chunks.title: Pelletron

chunks.text: The potential difference between the terminal and ground is used to accelerate several kinds of particles, such as positrons, electrons and negative and positive ions.

chunks.text: Strafing is the military practice of attacking ground targets from low-flying aircraft using aircraft-mounted automatic weapons ranging from machine guns (5mm to 20mm) to autocannons or rotary cannons (typically 20mm to 37mm).
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: This means that, although ground attack using automatic weapons fire is very often accompanied with bombing or rocket fire, the term "strafing" does not specifically include the last two.
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: The term "strafing" can cover either fixed guns, or aimable (flexible) guns.
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: Fixed guns firing directly ahead tend to be more predominant on fixed wing aircraft, while helicopters tend to use aimable weapons which can be fired in many different directions independent of the direction the aircraft is pointing in (in most cases, flexible guns on a fixed wing aircraft are for defense purposes only, although they can sometimes be used to fire on ground targets to limited effect).
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: Some fixed wing aircraft, like fighter-bombers, are capable of flying either air-combat missions or ground attack missions (P-47 Thunderbolt), while others are dedicated ground-attack types (Il-2 Shturmovik).
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: In cases where an aircraft is capable of both types of combat, when it is assigned to a ground attack role, and thus expected to be using the guns mostly for strafing, the fixed weapons are often mounted so that the convergence point is lower and at a greater range than would be used for air combat.
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: This is helpful because it allows the pilot to aim at a target without having to dive towards the ground as steeply, decreasing the risk of collision with the ground and increasing the amount of firing time available before having to pull up, and it also increases the range from the target, helping avoid anti-aircraft fire and potential damage from exploding targets.
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: Because of the low altitude and relatively low airspeed required for accurate strafing, it is very risky for the pilot, who is exposed not only to the risk of flight-into-terrain and obstacles such as power lines, but also to anti-aircraft weapons, including surface-to-air missiles (both vehicle mounted and hand-held), anti-aircraft artillery and small caliber weapons fire (such as machine guns and small arms).
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: Planes purposely designed for ground attack may include additional armour around and underneath the cockpit and other vulnerable areas such as engines to protect the pilot and key flight components, while aircraft designed mostly for air combat tend to have most of their armor placed to protect directly ahead or to the rear, where fire from other aircraft is most likely, leaving them more vulnerable to fire from directly below or to the sides, where much ground fire often comes from.
chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: Flextime (also spelled flexitime [British English], flex-time) is a flexible hours schedule that allows workers to alter workday start and finish times.
chunks.title: Flextime

chunks.text: In contrast to traditional work arrangements that require employees to work a standard 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. day, flextime typically involves a "core" period of the day during which employees are required to be at work (e.g., between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.), and a "bandwidth" period within which all required hours must be worked (e.g., between 5:30 a.m. and 7:30 p.m.).
chunks.title: Flextime

chunks.text: The working day outside of the "core" period is "flexible time", in which employees can choose when they work, subject to achieving total daily, weekly or monthly hours within the "bandwidth" period set by employers, and subject to the necessary work being done .
chunks.title: Flextime

chunks.text: The total working time required of employees on flextime schedules is the same as that required under traditional work schedules.
chunks.title: Flextime

chunks.text: A flextime policy allows staff to determine when they will work, while a flexplace policy allows staff to determine where they will work.
chunks.title: Flextime

chunks.text: Advantages include allowing employees to coordinate their work hours with public transport schedules, with the schedules of their children, and with daily traffic patterns to avoid high congestion times such as rush hour.
chunks.title: Flextime

chunks.text: Some claim that flexible working will change the nature of the way we work.

chunks.text: Wikisource is an online digital library of free content textual sources on a wiki, operated by the Wikimedia Foundation.
chunks.title: Wikisource

chunks.text: Wikisource is the name of the project as a whole and the name for each instance of that project (each instance usually representing a different language); multiple Wikisources make up the overall project of Wikisource.
chunks.title: Wikisource

chunks.text: The project's aims are to host all forms of free text, in many languages, and translations.
chunks.title: Wikisource

chunks.text: Originally conceived as an archive to store useful or important historical texts (its first text was the "Déclaration universelle des Droits de l'Homme"), it has expanded to become a general-content library.
chunks.title: Wikisource

chunks.text: The project officially began in November 24, 2003 under the name Project Sourceberg, a play on the famous Project Gutenberg.
chunks.title: Wikisource

chunks.text: The name Wikisource was adopted later that year and it received its own domain name seven months later.
chunks.title: Wikisource

chunks.text: The project has come under criticism for lack of reliability but it is also cited by organisations such as the National Archives and Records Administration.
chunks.title: Wikisource

chunks.text: Project Dragonfly is an American educational project.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: It was initially designed to give children opportunities in inquiry based learning in the sciences.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: The project was started as a magazine and website produced by professors in the Western College Program at Miami University and the National Science Teachers Association with a grant from the National Science Foundation and assistance from the Center for Human Development, Learning, and Teaching at Miami University.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Project Dragonfly now reaches millions of people each year through inquiry-driven learning media, public exhibits and graduate programs worldwide.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Project Dragonfly's partnership programs have generated an Emmy-Award-winning PBS television series, teacher workshops, master's degrees, public science exhibits, and conservation and education programs worldwide.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Supported by the National Science Foundation, the project began in 1994 with the first national magazine to feature children's science investigations and discoveries.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Project Dragonfly's programs include Earth Expeditions global graduate courses for educators and other professionals, the Global Field Program (GFP) and Advanced Inquiry Program (AIP) master's degrees, and iSaveSpecies, which engages zoo visitors throughout the country in science and conservation action.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Project Dragonfly is based in the biology department at Miami University, a state university in Oxford, Ohio.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Miami was established in 1809 and is listed as one of the eight original Public Ivies.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Public Engagement Projects include: iSaveSpecies, Wild Research, DragonflyTV.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Graduate Credit Workshops include Earth Expeditions, Zoo Expeditions, and iDiscovery.
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: Master's Degree Programs include Global Field Program (GFP) and Advanced Inquiry Program (AIP), and Earth Expeditions (EE).
chunks.title: Dragonfly Project

chunks.text: The Settlers IV (German: "Die Siedler IV" ), released as The Settlers: Fourth Edition in North America, is a 2001 real-time strategy video game developed by Blue Byte and published by Ubi Soft Entertainment for Microsoft Windows.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV

chunks.title: The Settlers IV

chunks.title: The Settlers IV

chunks.text: Jones Falls Trail (typically abbreviated JFT) is a hiking and bicycling trail in Baltimore, Maryland.
chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail

chunks.text: It mostly runs along the length of the namesake Jones Falls, a major north–south stream in and north of the city that has long acted as a major transportation corridor for the city.
chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail

chunks.text: It also incorporates the bike path encircling Druid Hill Reservoir and its namesake park.
chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail

chunks.text: The Jones Falls Trail forms a segment of the East Coast Greenway, a partially completed network of off-road bicycling routes that runs the length of the East Coast.
chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail

chunks.text: M-1, commonly known as Woodward Avenue, is a north–south state trunkline highway in the Metro Detroit area of the US state of Michigan.
chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)

chunks.text: The highway, called "Detroit's Main Street", runs from Detroit north-northwesterly to Pontiac.
chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)

chunks.text: It is one of the five principal avenues of Detroit, along with Michigan, Grand River, Gratiot, and Jefferson avenues.
chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)

chunks.text: These streets were platted in 1805 by Judge Augustus B. Woodward, namesake to Woodward Avenue.
chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)

chunks.text: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) has listed the highway as the Automotive Heritage Trail, an All-American Road in the National Scenic Byways Program.
chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)

chunks.text: It has also been designated a Pure Michigan Byway by the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT), and was also included in the MotorCities National Heritage Area designated by the US Congress in 1998.
chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)

chunks.text: The Nathan F. Cobb was a three-masted schooner named after the shipbuilder and founder of Cobb’s Salvaging Company whose many rescues of stranded ships help lead to the formation of the United States Life-Saving Service.
chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb

chunks.text: Despite its namesake's history of shipwreck rescues, the "Nathan F. Cobb" capsized in heavy seas on 1 December 1896 en route from Brunswick, Georgia to New York with a cargo of timber and cross ties.
chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb

chunks.text: The cook and a shipmate drowned when they were swept overboard in violent seas.
chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb

chunks.text: The crew righted the vessel by removing the three masts and they drifted for four days until they became grounded on a sandbar off Ormond Beach, Florida.
chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb

chunks.text: Rescue attempts led to the drowning of volunteer Ferd Waterhouse, whose body was never recovered, but no other crew members were lost.
chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb

chunks.text: A plaque commemorates Ferd Waterhouse’s rescue efforts.
chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb

chunks.text: The Cobb Cottage, a structure built using materials salvaged from the ship, is part of Ormond Beach’s Historic Trail.
chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb

chunks.text: Gurnee School District 56 is a PK-8 school district located in the northern Lake County village of the school district's namesake: Gurnee, Illinois.

chunks.text: Gurnee School District 56 is composed of four schools; three schools run in succession to the other, while the other services all nine grades.
chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.text: Spaulding feeds into Prairie Trail School, which educates third, fourth, and fifth graders.
chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.text: Kevin Simmons is the school's principal.Sheryl Gray is the assistant principal at Prairie Trail.
chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.text: The last section that this branch of the district's education can provide is to sixth, seventh, and eighth graders at Viking Middle School, whose principal is Patrick Jones.
chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.text: Viking is renowned for its wonderful drama and arts programs, along with its beautiful architecture.
chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.text: Viking Middle feeds into Warren Township High School in Gurnee, Illinois.
chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.text: The current Viking School was completed in 1998 after a flood rendered the old building unusable.
chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56

chunks.text: The United States Congress designated the Bell Mountain Wilderness in 1980.
chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness

chunks.text: The wilderness area now has a total of 9027 acre .
chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness

chunks.text: Bell Mountain is located within the Potosi-Fredericktown Ranger District of the Mark Twain National Forest, south of Potosi, Missouri in the United States.
chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness

chunks.text: The wilderness lies in the Saint Francois Mountains and it was named after its highest point, Bell Mountain (elevation: 1,702).
chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness

chunks.text: The namesake Bell Mountain has the name of Henry Bell, a pioneer settler.
chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness

chunks.text: The area is popular for hiking as there are 12 mi of trail, including a section of the Ozark Trail.
chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness

chunks.text: Pre's Trail, located on the north side of the Willamette River in Eugene, Oregon, United States, popularly referred to as "Track Town USA", is a four-mile-long running and walking trail named after heralded University of Oregon athlete Steve Prefontaine.

chunks.title: Pre's Trail

chunks.title: Pre's Trail

chunks.text: The Capital Area Greenbelt is a looping trail located in the area of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.
chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt

chunks.text: This 20-mile loop around Pennsylvania's capital city provides visitors and tourists with opportunities to hike, ride bicycles, skate, jog, fish, walk their dogs, enjoy native flora and fauna, and appreciate nature.
chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt

chunks.text: While parts of the trail are shared with roads, most of the loop is a dedicated path.
chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt

chunks.text: Asmodeus ( ; Greek: Ασμοδαίος , "Asmodaios") or Ashmedai ( ; Hebrew: אַשְמְדּאָי‎ ‎ , "ʾAšmədʾāy"; see below for other variations) is a "king of demons" mostly known from the deuterocanonical Book of Tobit, in which he is the primary antagonist.
chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.text: The demon is also mentioned in some Talmudic legends; for instance, in the story of the construction of the Temple of Solomon.
chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.text: Asmodeus also is referred to as one of the seven princes of Hell.
chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.text: In Binsfeld's classification of demons, each one of these princes represents one of the seven deadly sins (Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Sloth, Wrath, Envy, and Pride).
chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.text: Asmodeus is the demon of lust and is therefore responsible for twisting people's sexual desires, as seen in the book of Tobias especially.
chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.text: He is also said to be here on Earth after millions of years in hell.
chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.text: In Jewish and Islamic lore he is the king of the demons (Shedim/Jinn).
chunks.title: Asmodeus

chunks.text: Ballet is a formalized form of dance with its origins in the Italian Renaissance courts of the 15th and 16th centuries.

chunks.text: Aristocratic money was responsible for the initial stages of development in 'court ballet', as it was royal money that dictated the ideas, literature and music used in ballets that were created to primarily entertain the aristocrats of the time.

chunks.text: The first formal 'court ballet' ever recognized was staged in 1573, 'Ballet des Polonais'.

chunks.title: History of ballet

chunks.text: Catherine de' Medici and Balthasar de Beaujoyeulx were responsible for presenting the first court ballet ever to apply the principles of Baif's Academie, by integrating poetry, dance, music and set design to convey a unified dramatic storyline.
chunks.title: History of ballet

chunks.text: Moreover, the early organization and development of 'court ballet' was funded by, influenced by and produced by the aristocrats of the time, fulfilling both their personal entertainment and political propaganda needs.

chunks.text: The term "Anarchy at Samarra" refers to the period 861–870 in the history of the Abbasid Caliphate, which was marked by extreme internal instability and the violent succession of four caliphs, who became puppets in the hands of powerful rival military groups.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra

chunks.text: Musta'in was exiled and executed.
chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra

chunks.text: Mu'tazz was able and energetic, and tried to control the military chiefs and exclude the military from civil administration.

chunks.text: His policies were resisted, and in July 869 he too was deposed and killed.

chunks.text: Ernest Samuel McBride, Sr (November 20, 1909 – May 5, 2007) was an African American civil rights activist and community leader based in Long Beach, California.

chunks.title: Ernest McBride, Sr.

chunks.text: We passed the winter exhorting each other to faithfulness, while we anxiously waited for the accomplishment of the prophetic spirit of the revival.In the spring of 1780 we learned of a people near the city of Albany, NY, who were reported to have received a singular kind of religion, and that they possessed a large degree of divine light and spiritual power.

chunks.text: Many went out to see them and returned fully persuaded that they were the true witnesses of God.

chunks.text: The work increased and I felt a great desire to satisfy myself concerning these strangers and their religion.In June, in company with several others, I made them a visit.

chunks.text: We arrived on Saturday evening and remained till Monday.

chunks.text: We attended their meetings.

chunks.text: The singing was inspiring, the speaking powerful and heart-searching.

chunks.text: The wisdom of their instruction, the purity of their doctrine, and the Christ-like simplicity of their deportment all reminded me of the apostolic faith.

chunks.text: I saw that the work was of God, and my salvation depended upon it.The cross that was before me was an evidence of the spirit of the testimony.

chunks.text: On the one hand, the prospects of the world were flattering to my mind.
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: I was in the prime of life and in the vigor of health.
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: My reputation was fair, and my hopes not unpromising.On the other hand, religion had been my pursuit.
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: The revival had raised my hopes and directed my faith to a greater and more glorious work.
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: I subsequently made another visit and was received with kindness.
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: I confessed my sins to God, and with a fixed resolution accepted the cross of Christ.
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: I was now taught to rectify every wrong that I had committed, to forsake all sin and to take up a daily cross. "
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: I also became better acquainted with Mother Ann and the Elders who were with her, and am a witness of the purity of life which they constantly maintained.

chunks.text: The doctrine they taught was strictly conformable to the precepts and example of Jesus Christ.

chunks.text: By obeying their instruction I experienced the truth of their testimony.
chunks.title: Job Bishop

chunks.text: I was blessed with heavenly visions and felt my faith established on a sure foundation.I visited Mother Ann and the Elders many times at Watervliet, Harvard, Ashfield, Hancock, and New Lebanon, and freely associated with all the leading members of the Society.

chunks.text: Weighted correlation network analysis, also known as weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), is a widely used data mining method especially for studying biological networks based on pairwise correlations between variables.
chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis

chunks.text: While it can be applied to most high-dimensional data sets, it has been most widely used in genomic applications.
chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis

chunks.text: It allows one to define modules (clusters), intramodular hubs, and network nodes with regard to module membership, to study the relationships between co-expression modules, and to compare the network topology of different networks (differential network analysis).
chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis

chunks.text: WGCNA can be used as data reduction technique (related to oblique factor analysis ), as clustering method (fuzzy clustering), as feature selection method (e.g. as gene screening method), as framework for integrating complementary (genomic) data (based on weighted correlations between quantitative variables), and as data exploratory technique.
chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis

chunks.text: Although WGCNA incorporates traditional data exploratory techniques, its intuitive network language and analysis framework transcend any standard analysis technique.
chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis

chunks.text: Since it uses network methodology and is well suited for integrating complementary genomic data sets, it can be interpreted as systems biologic or systems genetic data analysis method.
chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis

chunks.text: By selecting intramodular hubs in consensus modules, WGCNA also gives rise to network based meta analysis techniques
chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis

chunks.text: In mathematics, specifically in homotopy theory, a classifying space "BG" of a topological group "G" is the quotient of a weakly contractible space "EG" (i.e. a topological space for which all its homotopy groups are trivial) by a proper free action of "G".
chunks.title: Classifying space

chunks.text: It has the property that any "G" principal bundle over a paracompact manifold is isomorphic to a pullback of the principal bundle "EG" → "BG".
chunks.title: Classifying space

chunks.text: As explained later, this means that classifying spaces represent a set-valued functor on the homotopy category of topological spaces.
chunks.title: Classifying space

chunks.text: The term classifying space can also be used for spaces that represent a set-valued functor on the category of topological spaces, such as Sierpiński space.
chunks.title: Classifying space

chunks.text: This notion is generalized by the notion of classifying topos.
chunks.title: Classifying space

chunks.text: However, the rest of this article discusses the more commonly used notion of classifying space up to homotopy.
chunks.title: Classifying space

chunks.text: Ecology is a new science and considered as an important branch of biological science, having only become prominent during the second half of the 20th century.

chunks.text: Blue is the second studio album by American rock band Third Eye Blind, released on November 23, 1999.

chunks.text: The album's creation was difficult, namely due to power struggles and arguments between frontman Stephan Jenkins and lead guitarist Kevin Cadogan, leading to a quick but isolated recording experience between members.

chunks.text: The Ford flathead V8 (often called simply the Ford flathead, flathead Ford, or flatty when the context is implicit, such as in hot-rodding) is a V8 engine of the valve-in-block type designed by the Ford Motor Company and built by Ford and various licensees.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: During the engine's first decade of production, when overhead-valve engines were rare, it was usually known simply as the Ford V‑8, and the first car model in which it was installed, the Model 18, was (and still is) often called simply the "Ford V‑8", after its new engine.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: Although the V8 configuration was not new when the Ford V8 was introduced in 1932, the latter was a market first in the respect that it made an 8-cylinder affordable and a V engine affordable to the emerging mass market consumer for the first time.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: It was the first independently designed and built V8 engine produced by Ford for mass production, and it ranks as one of the company's most important developments.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: A fascination with ever-more-powerful engines was perhaps the most salient aspect of the American car and truck market for a half century, from 1923 until 1973.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: The Ford flathead V8 was perfectly in tune with the cultural moment of its introduction, leading the way into a future of which the Ford company was a principal architect.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: Thus it became a phenomenal success.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: The engine design, with various changes but no major ones, was installed in Ford passenger cars and trucks until 1953, making the engine's 21-year production run for the U.S. consumer market longer than the 19-year run of the Ford Model T engine for that market.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: The engine was on Ward's list of the 10 best engines of the 20th century.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine

chunks.text: It was a staple of hot rodders in the 1950s, and it remains famous in the classic car hobbies even today, despite the huge variety of other popular V8s that followed.
chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
